issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named _detect_errors (leading underscore) but the template provides a function named detect_errors (no underscore). The reference solution also implements detect_errors. This naming mismatch between the problem description and the template will confuse students about which function to implement and may cause test harnesses to fail if they expect the underscored name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and tests to reference detect_errors (no underscore), or (B) rename the template and solution function to _detect_errors. Ensure the test names and task descriptions use the same identifier.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_detect_errors(...)` (leading underscore), but both the template and the reference solution implement the function as `detect_errors(...)` (no leading underscore). This naming mismatch can confuse students about which function to implement or test against, making it harder to map the textual task to the provided code skeleton and the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Prefer changing the problem statement to reference `detect_errors(...)` (remove the leading underscore) so it matches the template and solution. Alternatively, add a small compatibility alias in the template/solution (e.g. `_detect_errors = detect_errors`) so both names are accepted.
